summary: Heterogeneous GPU mix in dedicated pool causing unfair slot throttling and transient p50 throughput loss
description:
Issue summary: BrightCart reported intermittent p50 throughput regressions (20-35% increase) on their dedicated pool during off-peak hours starting 2026-03-01 02:10 UTC. Impact: customer-facing latency spikes for batched generation endpoints, elevated queue depth and fallback routing to lower-tier instances. Environment: BrightCart dedicated pool (heterogeneous GPU mix: some older A10G and newer A100s were present after a recent node re-provision).

Observed behaviour:
- Sudden p50 increase from 120ms -> 160-180ms for batched routes (batch size ~8).
- Autoscaler did not add new nodes for 7-9 minutes despite queue depth crossing the burst threshold.
- Single tenant (BrightCart) saw sustained throughput drop while other tenants on the same pool maintained normal throughput.
- GPU utilization graphs show apparent imbalance: older A10G nodes at 95% with growing NVLink wait spikes; A100 nodes showing lower sustained utilization but higher per-inference latency variance.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1. Send sustained batched traffic (batch=8, seq_len avg=512) to BrightCart dedicated route for 10 minutes.
2. Observe queue depth and p50/p95 on Redwood Console per-route dashboard.
3. Note autoscaler activity and slot allocation logs in the dedicated cluster.

Logs & links: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/brightcart/dedicated-pool-642981
Slack thread: #support (BrightCart) link t=thread-CLY2345
Instance logs: s3://redwood-logs/brightcart/2026-03-01/throughput/
Relevant tickets: SUP-33489 (slot fragmentation), INT-4123 (scheduler fairness experiment).

Immediate customer impact: Degraded user experience during intermittent windows; BrightCart flagged potential SLA breach and requested mitigation and RCA.

investigation_notes: Node inventory check: Maintenance on 2026-02-28 added three A10G nodes into the dedicated pool for capacity; node tagging inconsistency present (missing 'generation' tag on two nodes).

Scheduler logs: affinity_score calculation returned higher packing preference for older nodes for specific tenant CPU/memory footprint. Suspect integer overflow in weight adjustment when GPU_generation tag absent.

Autoscaler behavior: scale decision uses moving average of queue depth over 5 minutes — short burst did not exceed the high-water threshold long enough for immediate scale-out. Consider reducing window or adding spike-detection for dedicated pools.

Serving-runtime traces: on A10G nodes KV cache miss penalty slightly higher for long context; combined with higher tensor core divergence, effective per-batch GPU time increased leading to queue buildup.
Reproduction in lab: mixing a 30% subset of older nodes with batch-heavy tenant traffic reproduced 20-30% p50 regressions in 3/5 runs.
Related code areas: scheduler/packing.go, autoscaler/scale_policy.go, runtime/kernel_selector.cpp (PRs filed).
resolution_notes: 2026-03-03: Customer applied temporary route pinning to A100-only subset per support instructions — immediate p50 improvement observed.
2026-03-04: Deployed emergency scheduler change to prefer GPUs with 'generation' tag parity with tenant preference; this prevents cross-generation packing for routes with steady batch patterns.
2026-03-04: Short-term autoscaler adjustment applied: enable spike detector that triggers scale-out if queue depth > threshold for two consecutive 30s windows.
2026-03-04: Ops scheduled a tag-cleanup run for the pool to ensure generation metadata is present on all nodes to prevent affinity fallthrough.
Customer confirmation: BrightCart validated restored performance and reopened if regressions recur.
root_cause: Combination of mixed GPU generations in the dedicated pool and missing node metadata caused the scheduler affinity logic to preferentially pack a batch-heavy tenant onto older GPUs. Older GPUs had higher per-batch execution variance and NVLink wait spikes; autoscaler did not react quickly to the short-lived queue bursts because of a long averaging window. Together these produced transient p50 throughput loss for the tenant.
suggested_followups: Implement scheduler validation to reject ambiguous node metadata and surface warnings in Console on pool reconfiguration (owner: scheduler team, ETA 2 weeks).

Patch packing algorithm to account for GPU generation and per-node historical latency variance rather than relying on default affinity when tags missing (owner: runtime/scheduler, ETA 1 week for hotfix, 4 weeks for full test coverage).
Enhance autoscaler with a configurable short-burst detector for Dedicated pools (owner: autoscaler team, ETA 2 weeks).
Add an alert for mixed-GPU pools flagged as 'heterogeneous' with recommended placement policies for enterprise/dedicated customers (owner: ops/product, ETA 3 weeks).
Postmortem and customer-facing RCA doc to be published to Confluence and shared with BrightCart (owner: Support/Account, ETA 3 business days).
